title: One written degree can scope over a paired quality expression
summary: GDT810 gives five inherited paired-quality heads with one following value and a one-quality counterexample with two values. Test the narrower shared-degree reading: one written degree scopes over both qualities, rather than each repeated value being assigned to a separate quality.

design.mechanism: A paired quality expression can take one shared written degree/value, while repeated values are not evidence that each quality receives a separate degree.
design.unit: complete, reader-supported quality-head/value brackets with independently frozen one-quality versus paired-quality classification
design.contrast: shared degree over paired qualities versus one-value-per-quality allocation
design.prediction: Held paired-quality brackets should permit one value to qualify both qualities, while repeated values should be independently licensed by the construction rather than automatically mapped one-to-one to quality count; the separate-allocation model predicts a stable two-value requirement for paired heads.
design.falsifier: With an independently established quality pairing and value scope, paired heads systematically require two distinct values and single values cannot scope over both, falsifying the shared-degree model.
design.scope_note: The paired/single quality labels and value meanings are inherited working hypotheses, not independent semantic gold. This proposal does not revive GDT810's rejected general multiple-value prediction.
design.related: Source-specific successor to GDT810's arity screen, with the opposite narrow question (shared degree versus forced one-to-one allocation); adjacent to IDEA000048/000049 but not a comparison-standard or unit-calibration claim.
design.countermodel: A repeated value may reflect repetition, a second field, or an unrelated local construction; one shared value may also be underspecified rather than semantically shared. Both rivals can fit the motivating line without frozen scope coding.

source_evidence.quote:
The five paired-quality examples are `otchol daiin` on f5v.5 and f44v.2,
`otchol dain` on f7r.7, `kchol daiin` on f45r.3 and `tchol dain` on f47r.10.
These forms receive their one/two-quality classification from an inherited
hypothesis; the classification itself has not been independently decoded.

The counterexample to a quality-count explanation is f21v.4:

```text
sho chodaiin choty | chol daiin daiin | chty chtol
```

The central span and next word agree in all three alternative readings.
Here the old `chol` candidate has only one quality, dry, yet two values follow.
Thus repeated values are not unique to supposed two-quality compounds.

design.principal_risk: The source's inherited quality classification and bracket boundaries may not support independent scope annotation; repeated values may be unrelated to quality semantics.
